alignments.note: `כִּי` recast as a relative; the ASV rewrites that subordinator over the coordinated second colon, so both occurrences are this morpheme's one discontinuous unit, headed on the first (rule 55).

Light verb plus complement *is surety*, headed on the complement (rule 44), with the supplied *for* reaching the verb's bare object; the Hebrew writes this verb once and the ASV realizes it twice across the coordination, so both realizations are its one discontinuous unit (rules 34, 25).
Bare object noun with its own indefinite article (rule 15).
Imperative rendered as light verb plus complement *hold ... in pledge*, headed on the complement, discontinuous around the object pronoun.

review_notes: Variant WLC.PRO.20.16.v002 was resolved to r01, covering s009, which the ASV's *foreigners* matches; the textual note about *a foreign woman* was read and set aside (rule 38).

The italic *that is surety* was read as the second realization of the one written `עָרַב` (rule 34) with its subordinator rewritten under rule 55, rather than as an `added` supplied verb; the italics corroborate but do not decide (rule 7).
